title: Fate of the non-Abelian Moore-Read manifold under the non-Hermitian skin effect
authors: Jiaxuan Guo, Simin Nie, Xiting Zhang, Fritz B. Prinz
abstract: We study a non-Abelian Moore-Read fractional Chern insulator under a translation-preserving, nonreciprocal deformation that generates the non-Hermitian skin effect under open boundaries. The model combines the imaginary-gauge Hatano-Nelson deformation with a kagome-lattice three-body interaction designed to stabilize Moore-Read order at $ν=1/2$. Our primary diagnostic is the biorthogonal $(2,4)$-admissible particle-entanglement counting of the sixfold Moore-Read manifold, the standard Moore-Read fingerprint. Across three sizes ($N=16,20,24$), the counting locks to the clean references 1308, 3965, and 9282 over finite nonreciprocity windows through $γ\le0.55$, $0.65$, and $0.74$, respectively, with positive reference-rank entanglement gaps. Within every reported window the count is unchanged by the spectral readings tested; at $N=16$ it is also unchanged across three reduced density operators, with all 15 combinations returning 1308. The sixfold pattern for even $N_f$ and the adiabatically tracked Ising-odd doublet remain separated over the tested range $γ\le0.6$. Beyond a geometry-dependent threshold the instantaneous-lowest-six reference-rank gap drops sharply and its counting destabilizes. At $N=24$ a sector-0 branch pair becomes complex conjugate over a narrow interval inside the delocking bracket; both continuations through the interval are delocked at the tested PES points $γ=0.76$, $0.77$, and $0.80$. A same-lattice Abelian $ν=1/3$ Laughlin realization retains its counting to $γ=1.0$, so its counting is the more robust. On the torus the eigenstates remain extended; under open boundaries the right and left states skin-localize at opposite edges while the biorthogonal particle-entanglement spectrum is invariant under the imaginary-gauge similarity, so the torus and the open cylinder probe the same deformation under periodic and open boundaries.
summary: This paper analyzes the stability of the non-Abelian Moore-Read topological order when subjected to a non-Hermitian skin effect in a fractional Chern insulator model. Using particle-entanglement counting, the authors demonstrate that the topological signature remains robust over a finite range of nonreciprocity, although the Abelian counterpart proved more stable. This establishes a diagnostic tool for characterizing topological phases in open, non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how the non-Hermitian skin effect alters the topological order of a non-Abelian Moore-Read fractional Chern insulator.
main_result: The non-Abelian Moore-Read entanglement counting remains robust and locks to clean references over finite nonreciprocity windows, although the Abelian Laughlin state was found to be even more robust.
method: The analysis uses biorthogonal methods to solve the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian and diagnoses topological order via the biorthogonal (2, 4)-admissible particle-entanglement counting.
model_or_system: The model is a non-Abelian Moore-Read fractional Chern insulator realized on a kagome lattice, incorporating a Hatano-Nelson type imaginary-gauge deformation and a three-body interaction.
key_observables: Biorthogonal (2, 4)-admissible particle-entanglement counting (Moore-Read fingerprint), spectral gaps, and the persistence of the count versus the nonreciprocity parameter $\gamma$.
important_parameters:
Nonreciprocity parameter $\gamma$, system size $N$ ($16, 20, 24$), and the filling fraction $
u$ ($
u=1/2$ for Moore-Read, $
u=1/3$ for Laughlin).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on selecting the six lowest-Re energy eigen-pairs to define the ground-state manifold and the entanglement spectrum.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the imaginary-gauge deformation on the kagome lattice, the skin effect on single-particle eigenstates, and the entanglement-counting ratio remaining locked for the Moore-Read state over a finite window.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the non-Hermitian model and the diagnostic tool (PES counting), presents results showing the finite-size survival window for the Moore-Read count, compares it to the Abelian Laughlin state, and discusses the physical implications of the delocking threshold.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete theoretical framework for diagnosing topological order in open, non-Hermitian systems, which is highly relevant for understanding edge physics in synthetic quantum materials.
